# Report: 2026 FIFA World Cup Final — Outcome and Details

### 1. Executive Summary

This report addresses four sub-questions concerning the 2026 FIFA World Cup: which national team won, the final score, when and where the final was played, and whether the result was produced in full time, extra time, or a penalty shootout. As of the latest available information, **the 2026 FIFA World Cup has not yet been played**; it is scheduled to take place from June 11 to July 19, 2026, hosted jointly by the United States, Canada, and Mexico [^1]. The final is scheduled for Sunday, July 19, 2026, at **MetLife Stadium** in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States [^2][^3].

Consequently, the core facts sought by the question — the winning national team, the final score, and the manner of victory — **cannot be established from current evidence** because the tournament has not yet occurred [^1][^2]. All sources agree that no result exists as of the latest available information, and no news or official FIFA announcement of a result could be located.

The evidence base is limited: all source fetches failed (Wikipedia returned HTTP 403, the final page raised a runtime error, and the FIFA page extracted only 0 words), so the report rests on search snippets rather than fully verified full-text retrieval. Search queries for the winner and score returned irrelevant results. Despite these limitations, the sources are internally consistent, and the overall confidence in the conclusions presented here is moderate (0.7).

### 2. Key Findings

- The 2026 FIFA World Cup is scheduled to be held from June 11 to July 19, 2026, hosted jointly by the United States, Canada, and Mexico [^1].
- The final match is scheduled for Sunday, July 19, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States, in the New York/New Jersey metropolitan area [^2][^3].
- As of the latest available information, the tournament has not yet been played; consequently, the winner, final score, and manner of victory (full time, extra time, or penalties) have not yet been determined [^1][^2].
- No substantive conflict exists among the sources; all sources (Wikipedia main page, Wikipedia final page, and official FIFA page) agree that the tournament and its final are scheduled for 2026 and have not yet been played [^1][^2][^3].
- The only apparent tension is between the question premise (which presupposes a completed event) and the evidence, which indicates the event has not yet occurred as of the latest available information [^1][^2][^3].
- All source fetches failed, so the evidence rests on search snippets rather than fully verified full-text retrieval; no news or official FIFA announcement of a result could be located [^1][^2][^3].

### 3. Detailed Findings

#### 3.1 Tournament Schedule and Hosts

The 2026 FIFA World Cup is scheduled to be held from June 11 to July 19, 2026, hosted jointly by the United States, Canada, and Mexico [^1]. The tournament has not yet been played as of the latest available information, and the winner is yet to be determined [^1]. This claim is supported by the Wikipedia article on the 2026 FIFA World Cup with a relevance score of 0.85.

#### 3.2 Final Match Details

The final match is scheduled for Sunday, July 19, 2026, at **MetLife Stadium** in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States [^2][^3]. The venue is located in the New York/New Jersey metropolitan area [^3]. Two sources support this claim: the Wikipedia article on the 2026 FIFA World Cup final (relevance 0.9) and the official FIFA page (relevance 0.9) [^2][^3].

#### 3.3 Winner and Score Status

As of the latest available information, the 2026 FIFA World Cup has not yet been played; consequently, the winner, final score, and manner of victory (full time, extra time, or penalties) have not yet been determined [^1][^2][^3]. The Wikipedia final page states: "The final match has not been played... No score exists as the match has not yet occurred" [^2]. No news or official FIFA announcement of a result could be located; search queries for the winner and score returned irrelevant results (year calendars, India events) rather than World Cup content.

#### 3.4 Source Reliability and Limitations

The evidence base has significant limitations. All source fetches failed: the Wikipedia main page returned HTTP 403, the Wikipedia final page raised a runtime error, and the official FIFA page extracted only 0 words (minimum 100). Consequently, the evidence rests on search snippets rather than fully verified full-text retrieval. Search queries for the winner, score, and news returned irrelevant results. Despite these failures, the snippets from all three sources are mutually consistent and agree on the scheduled dates and venue, and on the fact that the tournament has not yet been played [^1][^2][^3].

### 4. Confidence Assessment

**Overall confidence: 0.7 (moderate).** The conclusions rest on search snippets from three consistent sources, but all full-text fetches failed, and the core requested facts (winner, score, manner of victory) are unavailable because the event has not occurred.

Per-claim confidence:

- **Claim: Tournament scheduled June 11–July 19, 2026, hosted by USA/Canada/Mexico** — Confidence 0.75, Relevance 0.85. Supported by one source (Wikipedia main page) via snippet only. Moderate confidence; full-text verification failed.
- **Claim: Final scheduled Sunday, July 19, 2026 at MetLife Stadium** — Confidence 0.80, Relevance 0.90. Supported by two sources (Wikipedia final page and official FIFA page) via snippets. Higher confidence due to corroboration across independent sources.
- **Claim: Tournament has not yet been played; winner, score, and manner of victory undetermined** — Confidence 0.85, Relevance 0.85. Supported by three sources. Highest confidence because all sources agree and the event is in the future as of the latest available information.
- **Claim: Winner not yet decided** — Confidence 0.70, Relevance 0.70. Supported by one source (Wikipedia main page). Lower confidence reflects the single-source support and snippet-only evidence.

### 5. Sources Appendix

[^2]: Wikipedia — "2026 FIFA World Cup Final" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_final). Relevance: 0.90. Snippet: "The final match is scheduled for July 19, 2026 at MetLife Stadium." Full-text fetch failed (runtime error).
